title: Country bands in Napoleonville area, then move to Kit Harris
summary: Playing with Joseph Gabriel's ten-piece band and the James brothers in the country, getting his trombone at twenty and coming to New Orleans to join Kit Harris.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: He was what you call a fellow, he couldn't see at night but he could just make out in the day. And he was a wonderful violin player. He used to come by my mother when we'd get new music like that. She'd play the melody on the piano and he had a real good ear, but he couldn't see the music at all. But he was a fine fellow. And then from there I played a couple of dates with Professor Clevon Williams and his band. Then later on, after I married, my son was born, I played with a fellow in Tippet-Owe by the name of Joseph Gabriel. They call him Gabriel, but some people say Gabriel, but we call him Gabriel. He was also, he had about a ten piece orchestra. He used to play all down by a place named Luke. He played at the big pavilion in Homer. Well, he had quite a bit of work. He kept me going Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays.
Do you remember Lewis James, the bass player? Sure, sure. Was he from there? I think he told us.

He's from Tippet-Owe. He had Lewis James and he had two other brothers. One played clarinet. Well, you know Lewis James instrument was tenor sax and clarinet. Yes. And he just, I think he just got on the bass since he came here in New Orleans.
Yes, I believe he told us about these Gabriel.

Yeah, and then he had another brother named Pallet. He was a trombone player and he went to the bass. Then he had another brother named Willie. Well, he played saxophone and clarinet. They all used to play with Joe Gabriel, but they had some kind of falling out and they organized the James brothers band out there in Tippet-Owe. And then from there I came down to New Orleans.
Well, how old were you when you got your trombone about?
Yeah, and I came down here to New Orleans and I got with a fellow by the name of Kit Harris. You might have heard of him.
